summary: Bidirectional alignment is nearly complete and solver-visible contracts are well-formed, but recovery of committed DELETE mutations across process restart is a material instruction requirement with no meaningful behavioral test. A solver could omit durable DELETE WAL replay and still pass all 63 probes.

findings.criterion: Every material requirement has meaningful behavioral test coverage (forward matrix completeness)
findings.why_it_matters: Instruction requires recovery to retain every valid committed transaction and documents DELETE WAL records, but no probe commits a DELETE and restarts (with or without checkpoint) to verify the deletion survives durability/recovery. An implementation that applies DELETE only in-memory or fails to replay DELETE frames would pass all current tests.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add at least one restart probe that seeds a key, commits a DELETE, restarts the engine, and asserts NOT_FOUND/empty scan plus correct sequence; optionally add an independently encoded DELETE+COMMIT WAL fixture mirroring the existing PUT fixture.
findings.regression_risk: Low if added as a new preservation or contract probe without weakening existing corruption or conflict checks.

findings.why_it_matters: Storage-format declares zero-byte declared WAL payload length as intrinsic corruption, but no probe supplies a complete header with payload_length=0; this is a narrow framing edge unlike the DELETE recovery gap.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional: add a corruption probe with a complete zero-length framing header expecting fail-closed open.

UNTESTED_REQUIREMENTS: R08: Recovery of a committed DELETE transaction across process restart (WAL replay and/or post-checkpoint snapshot reload) — instruction.md:12 and storage-format.md DELETE payload type are solver-visible but no probe restarts after a successful DELETE commit.
